Build the 26-connected voxel graph of a binary skeleton: (points, neighbor lists, degree).

nvitk.measure.morpho.skeleton.skeletonize_mask(mask_bool: numpy.ndarray) → numpy.ndarray¶

Thin a binary mask to its 1-voxel-wide skeleton (skimage medial-axis skeletonize).

nvitk.measure.morpho.skeleton.skeleton_tree_from_mask(mask_bool: numpy.ndarray, spacing=None, length_scale: float = 1.0) → nvitk.measure.morpho.models.SkeletonTree¶

Skeletonize mask_bool, optionally prune short terminal spurs, and build a SkeletonTree.

length_scale rescales the human-calibrated spur threshold for other species (see _meta.length_scale in the topology JSON).

nvitk.measure.morpho.skeleton.prune_short_terminal_spurs(skel: numpy.ndarray, max_len_mm: float, spacing=None) → numpy.ndarray¶

Erase terminal spur branches shorter than max_len_mm that end at a real branchpoint.

Iterates to convergence since removing one spur can expose another; spurs that connect two true endpoints (not a branchpoint) are left alone so short vessels aren’t deleted.

nvitk.measure.morpho.skeleton.find_loop_branches(pts: numpy.ndarray, neighbors: List[List[int]], degree: numpy.ndarray)¶

Detect simple donut/cycle topologies in a skeleton graph.

Returns:

nodes participating in at least one cycle. gateways: branchpoints where the loop connects to the rest of the tree. loops: list of (gateway_a, gateway_b, arm1_node_indices, arm2_node_indices).

Return type:

cycle_core

nvitk.measure.morpho.skeleton.dijkstra_dist_from_root(tree: nvitk.measure.morpho.models.SkeletonTree, root: int, spacing) → numpy.ndarray¶

Physical (mm) shortest-path distance from root to every skeleton node.

Plain O(n²) Dijkstra without a heap — skeleton graphs here are small enough that this is simpler and fast enough than a priority-queue implementation.
